prerequisites: Preliminary knowledge of geometry (e.g., improper elements of plane and space, concept of distance, plane transformations, conic curves)

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding the basic principles of representation and the ability to choose the most appropriate method.
Understanding the notions of geometry applied to representation methods.
Knowledge of standardization and unification aspects; ability to autonomously research and interpret technical standards.
Knowledge of various types of technical drawing (assembly, detail) and their constituent elements (views, sections, dimensions, tolerances, and annotations).

Knowledge of the main classes of standardized mechanical components and their conventional representation (threads, nuts, screws, shaft/hub connections, bearings, and gears); autonomous ability to identify such components from catalogs/standards.
Ability to interpret indications related to dimensional and geometric tolerances and surface finish requirements.
Ability to interpret drawings in relation to functional and manufacturing requirements.
Ability to read and interpret diagrams.
Knowledge and understanding applied to the creation of technical drawings using two-dimensional CAD software.

syllabus_topics: Industry and training situation in Italy and the world: an overview
Introduction to technical drawing and its historical evolution
Fundamentals of descriptive geometry. Historical evolution, central projections and parallel projections.
Orthogonal projections, views and their arrangement in drawing
Reading diagrams, graphical representation of data and processes
Use of two-dimensional CAD software for technical drawing
teaching_methods: Laboratory exercises using two-dimensional CAD software

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical test (multiple-choice questionnaire via LIbreEOL platform)
Practical test (execution of a graphic work on the computer)

assessment_rules: The final grade is the arithmetic mean of the evaluations obtained in the two tests. To pass the exam, it is necessary to obtain a positive evaluation (18/30 or higher) in both tests. Unless otherwise specified, the two tests take place on the same day, one after the other.
